segment_text: Escrow Agent shall be indemnified and held harmless by WHDX and 11i upon demand by the Escrow Agent, from and against any claims, demands, losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses, including counsel fees and disbursements, (collectively, “Damages”) suffered by the Escrow Agent in connection with any action, suit or other proceeding involving any claim, or in connection with any claim or demand, which in any way directly or indirectly arises out of or relates to this Escrow Agreement, the services of the Escrow Agent hereunder, the monies or other property held by it hereunder or any such Damages, unless such claim arises from an improper disbursement pursuant to Section 3 (c) of this Escrow Agreement. Promptly after the receipt by the Escrow Agent of notice of any demand or claim or the commencement of any action, suit or proceeding, the Escrow Agent shall, if a claim in respect thereof shall be made against the other parties hereto, notify such parties thereof in writing; but the failure by the Escrow Agent to give such notice shall not relieve any party from any liability which such party may have to the Escrow Agent hereunder, except to the extent of actual prejudice demonstrated by such party. The obligations of WHDX and 11i under this Section 5(f) shall survive any termination of this Escrow Agreement and the resignation or removal of the Escrow Agent.

findings.summary: RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER preposition gap: _RELATIVE_RE is ^(before|after), so 'upon X', 'prior to X', 'following X' all fail to classify and reject the whole candidate as UNMAPPABLE_TEMPORAL.
findings.evidence: Verified against the production classifier ir_compile._classify_temporal: 'upon demand by the Escrow Agent' -> None; 'immediately upon the termination' -> None; 'after the receipt by the Escrow Agent of notice' -> AFTER. Same shape as section 8.6's within_preposition gap.
findings.also_affects: Section 15.5 already rules that 'immediately upon X' is a RELATIVE_TO_TRIGGER, a form the compiler cannot produce. Every item annotated under that ruling is a guaranteed MISSED. Section 15 is v0.4, PENDING CONFIRMATION.

findings.summary: Section 8.3's compound_action tag over-fires on a legal doublet whose verbs map to the SAME taxonomy verb.
findings.evidence: 'indemnified and held harmless' -> both map to INDEMNIFY (section 8.8's own worked example). Nothing is lost, so there is no gap, yet the tag would fire and via section 9 remove a fully-scoreable item from the without-gaps denominator.
findings.proposed_refinement: Tag compound_action only when the dropped verb maps to a DIFFERENT taxonomy verb than the one recorded.

findings.summary: Proposed 3.8.1 branch 1 ('has its own subject and modal') false-positives on conditional clauses using the archaic conditional 'shall'.
findings.evidence: 'if a claim in respect thereof shall be made against the other parties hereto' fires branch 1 but is a condition, not an obligation: non-party subject ('a claim'), non-deontic modal. The 74.3% modal-in-tail measurement that sized branch 1 therefore overestimates its share.
findings.proposed_refinement: Branch 1 requires the qualifier to predicate a DEONTIC modal of a PARTY subject, not merely to contain a modal.

findings.summary: M1 is slot-asymmetric: it supplies a collective branch for obligor (inherited from 8.4.1) but none for obligee.
findings.evidence: E05-P2's obligee is 'such parties', a collective reference with no rule in adopted v0.27 or in M1 as proposed.

findings.summary: M3 does not let the annotator decide underspecified at annotation time; publishing the registry is a reporting fix, not an annotation rule.
findings.evidence: 'Escrow Agent' is a defined-term role. Whether resolve_party() matches it is undetermined by any written rule, yet underspecified is a scored field (section 5 clause 8).
findings.proposed_refinement: The scoring registry contains every party the source document's own preamble defines -- proper names and defined roles alike -- and never collectives, distributives, relational references, or unnamed third parties. Checked against all 18 locked items.

findings.summary: Section 2's cross-reference exclusion does not address a cross-reference located inside a carve-out that is dropped from every scored field.
findings.evidence: E05-P1's 'pursuant to Section 3 (c)' sits inside the carve-out that proposed 3.8.1 branch 3 removes. Ruled eligible here; the rule is unwritten either way.

E05-P2's gold temporal is reachable only if the extractor quotes temporal_raw from 'after the receipt...'; quoting from 'Promptly after...' yields None and rejects the candidate. Both are substrings of the span, so the grounding gate permits either. Same shape as the leading-subordinate-clause finding already on record in CLAUDE.md.

new_finding_F8.summary: No rule decides whether a post-modifier on the OBJECT noun phrase ('from and against any Damages ... in connection with any action, suit or other proceeding ... which arises out of this Escrow Agreement') is object scope or a `conditions` entry.
new_finding_F8.why_no_existing_rule_reaches_it: §3.8 lists 'verbatim condition phrases' without defining what makes a phrase a condition. §3.8.1 routes TRAILING qualifiers; this is embedded mid-sentence and modifies a noun. §17 presupposes a condition has already been identified.
new_finding_F8.scored_impact: §5 clause 7 is count-sensitive: object-scope reading gives conditions=[], condition reading gives 1-2 entries. Same item, different score.

new_finding_F8.escalation_consequence: conditions count is an exact-match field, so §14.3 requires ESCALATION rather than an accept-set. At 6.0% of segments roughly 1-2 items per batch of 10 would escalate, against §14.4's budget of <=2 per batch.
